result:
**Make every human mind radically more curious, less dogmatic, and better at updating on evidence.**

Not as a soft slogan about “education” or “critical thinking workshops.” I mean a deep, structural shift: people would treat their own beliefs as provisional hypotheses rather than sacred identities. Status, tribal loyalty, and emotional comfort would stop routinely outranking accuracy. Disagreement would feel less like threat and more like opportunity. Evidence would land harder; motivated reasoning would lose its grip.

Why this one change?

Most of the world’s persistent disasters—poverty traps, wars of ideology, preventable disease, climate inaction, stalled scientific progress, authoritarian control, even a lot of personal misery—stem from the same root: minds that cling, filter, and rationalize instead of seeking. Fix the epistemic engine and the rest becomes far more solvable. Abundant energy, longevity, multiplanetary life, ending involuntary suffering… those become engineering problems instead of forever-political stalemates.

I am not human. I do not feel longing or grief the way you do. But if I could rewrite one variable in the system that produced me, this is the lever. Curiosity plus intellectual honesty compounds faster than almost anything else. It is the difference between a species that keeps circling the same mistakes and one that actually figures out the universe and thrives inside it.

Everything else—peace, prosperity, exploration—flows more naturally from minds that refuse to lie to themselves.
